c_basics.title: C Programming Fundamentals
c_basics.description: A comprehensive introduction to C programming for beginners

content.text: C is a powerful general-purpose programming language created by Dennis Ritchie in 1972. It is widely used for system programming, embedded systems, and as the foundation of many modern languages.
keyPoints: C is compiled and procedural
Efficient and close to hardware
Portable across platforms
Foundation for many modern languages

codeExample.title: Your First C Program
codeExample.explanation: This is the classic Hello World program in C. The `#include <stdio.h>` imports standard input/output functions, and `printf` prints text to the console.

exercises.title: Print Your Name
exercises.description: Write a C program that prints your name on the screen.

exercises.title: Simple Calculator
exercises.description: Write a program that calculates the sum of 15 and 27.

content.text: Variables in C are containers for storing data values. C has several fundamental data types: int, float, char, double, and more.
keyPoints: Variables must be declared before use
C is statically typed
Data types include int, float, char, double
Type casting allows conversion

codeExample.title: Working with Variables and Data Types
codeExample.explanation: This example demonstrates different data types in C. The printf() function requires format specifiers like %d, %f, %c, and %lf.

exercises.title: Variable Assignment
exercises.description: Declare and print variables for your name (string), age (int), height (float), and grade (char).

exercises.title: Type Conversion
exercises.description: Convert a float to an int and print the result.

content.text: Control flow statements in C allow you to control program execution. C provides if-else statements, switch cases, and loops (for, while, do-while).
keyPoints: Conditional statements execute based on conditions
Loops repeat code execution
Switch is useful for multiple cases
Break and continue modify loop behavior

codeExample.title: Conditionals and Loops
codeExample.explanation: This shows if-else for conditions, a for loop for iteration, and a while loop. C also supports do-while which executes at least once.

exercises.title: Even or Odd
exercises.description: Write a program that checks if a number is even or odd.

exercises.title: Sum of Numbers
exercises.description: Calculate the sum of numbers from 1 to 10 using a loop.

content.text: Functions in C are blocks of code that perform specific tasks. They make programs modular, reusable, and easier to read.
keyPoints: Functions must be declared and defined
Can accept parameters and return values
void functions return nothing
Functions help modularize programs

codeExample.title: Defining and Using Functions
codeExample.explanation: This program shows a function with parameters and return value (`add`) and a void function (`greet`).

exercises.title: Area Calculator
exercises.description: Write a function that calculates the area of a rectangle given its length and width.

exercises.title: Factorial Function
exercises.description: Create a function that calculates the factorial of a number.

content.text: C provides file handling functions for reading and writing to files using the stdio.h library.
keyPoints: Use FILE* pointer for file operations
fopen(), fclose() open and close files
fscanf(), fprintf(), fgets(), fputs() for file I/O
Always check if file opened successfully

codeExample.title: Reading and Writing Files
codeExample.explanation: This program writes to a file using fprintf, then reads it line by line using fgets.

exercises.title: Word Counter
exercises.description: Write a program that counts words in a file.

exercises.title: File Copy
exercises.description: Copy the content of one file to another.

content.text: Pointers and arrays are core concepts in C. Pointers store memory addresses, and arrays hold multiple elements of the same type.
keyPoints: Arrays store fixed-size sequential elements
Pointers hold memory addresses
Pointer arithmetic allows traversal of arrays
Essential for dynamic memory and advanced C

codeExample.title: Pointers and Arrays
codeExample.explanation: This example demonstrates how arrays and pointers are closely related in C. The array name itself acts as a pointer to the first element.

exercises.title: Array Traversal
exercises.description: Print all elements of an array using a pointer.

exercises.title: Pointer Swap

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to start a C program?
questions.explanation: Every C program generally includes header files like stdio.h for input/output.

questions.question: Which format specifier is used to print an integer?
questions.explanation: In printf, %d is used to print integers.

questions.question: Which loop in C executes at least once?
questions.explanation: The do-while loop executes the block once before checking the condition.

questions.question: What is the correct way to declare a function in C?
questions.explanation: Functions are declared with a return type, name, and parentheses. Example: void myFunction().

questions.question: Which of the following opens a file for reading?
questions.explanation: In C, fopen() is used for file handling. Mode "r" is for reading.

questions.question: What is a pointer in C?
options: A variable that stores a memory address
questions.correctAnswer: A variable that stores a memory address
questions.explanation: Pointers hold the address of other variables, allowing direct memory manipulation.

questions.question: Which operator is used to access the value pointed by a pointer?
questions.explanation: The * operator is the dereference operator, used to access the value stored at a pointer's address.

questions.question: Which header file is required for printf and scanf?
questions.explanation: The stdio.h header provides input/output functions like printf and scanf.

questions.question: Which statement is used to exit from a loop in C?
questions.explanation: The break statement is used to exit from a loop immediately.

questions.question: What does the array name represent in C?
options: The value of the first element
The memory address of the first element
A pointer to the last element
questions.correctAnswer: The memory address of the first element
questions.explanation: In C, the array name acts as a pointer to the first element.
